Anna Liu: Drafting a PRD fragment for dedicated capacity: graceful degradation, warm-pool autoscale, and acceptance criteria for SLAs. 👇
Anna Liu: Goal: define exact tests + edge cases so product + SRE can sign off. Link to draft: https://docs.redwood.example/drafts/graceful-degrade (please comment)
Anna Liu: Main asks: (1) how we measure p95 (server-side vs end-to-end), (2) acceptable throughput per-GPU for default quantized models, (3) autoscale cooldowns and warmpool sizing, (4) rollback triggers for canary fails.
Raj Patel: For clarity — are we measuring p95 on request completion (include token generation) or on first-byte?
Anna Liu: Server-side request completion (including generation) excluding client-side streaming latencies. Retries excluded from p95 calculation.
Maria Gomez: Please add a partial-GPU-failure scenario (e.g., one card loses 30% of memory / OOMs). We need target behavior: route subset of traffic off degraded node + warmpool spin-up.
Kevin O'Neill: Can we put concrete throughput numbers in the doc? engineering needs a formula + sample numbers for sizing.
Anna Liu: Draft sizing formula (pseudo):
```
effective_qps = floor(gpu_flops_factor * model_factor * seq_len_factor / safety_headroom)
warmpool_target = ceil(expected_peak_qps / effective_qps * 0.2)  // 20% warm spare
```
Sample (gpt-medium-16k): effective_qps ~ 120 qps per A100-80GB quant profile at avg seq=512.
Samir Kaur: Autoscale notes: minimum scale step = 1 node, cooldown = 90s, max spin-up parallelism = 3 nodes. Warmpool spin-up should be prioritized ahead of on-demand cold nodes.
SRE-Bot: [load-test-ci #742] synthetic load: sustained 80% target load, p95=312ms, errors=0.6% (2024-11-05T14:02Z).
Raj Patel: SLA credit calc: we should add explicit formula in PRD. e.g. credits = floor((allowed_minutes - met_minutes) / 60). Need product to confirm compensation policy.
Anna Liu: Acceptance criteria (proposed):
1) Under sustained target load (90% of provisioned) p95 <= 350ms for standard small models, <= 700ms for 16k models.
2) Error rate < 1% sustained.
3) Canary pass = zero OOMs + no more than 2% p95 regression vs baseline.
4) Warmpool can return to ready < 45s 90% of time.
5) Partial-GPU-loss flow: traffic shifted away from degraded node within 12s, no customer-level SLA breach if fallback kicks in.
(put these into the PRD checklist)
Maria Gomez: Edge-case: queued requests during a rolling model swap. We should document max queue time (we recommend 30s) and fallback to lower-cost variant if queue > threshold. Also KV cache invalidation TTLs need a callout.
Kevin O'Neill: Launch gating timeline question: what metrics do we need from stress runs?
Anna Liu: Launch gates:
- 3 independent stress runs across regions with sustained load >= 95% of projected peak for 2h
- p95 within acceptance window across all runs
- Incident-free canary for 48h (no production-level rollbacks)
- Headroom >= 15% for sudden 2x spike for 5m window
- Rollback plan tested (automated revert)
If all green -> GA.
Samir Kaur: I can build a harness that simulates queued requests + degraded GPU behavior (will reuse redis queue + tox test harness). Will post PR with config tomorrow.
SRE-Bot: Follow-up: scheduling a 30m sync Friday 10:00 to review PRD acceptance wording and finalize numbers. @Anna Liu @Raj Patel @Maria Gomez @Kevin O'Neill @Samir Kaur
Anna Liu: Thanks — please add any comments inline on the draft, especially around the warmpool sizing heuristic and the SLA credit formula. :thumbsup:
